episodes.summary: Maha introduces his father Charat to his very young son.
episodes.boundary: Family relationship is historical; setting, words, gestures, objects and conversation are authored

episodes.summary: Charat married Desan, Amir Singh daughter, and the families joined resources at Gujranwala.
episodes.boundary: A household recollection is authored; do not assert that Ranjit personally met Desan, or resolve the disputed mother/stepmother wording
episodes.authored_theme: Remember household leadership alongside military command

episodes.summary: Charat and allied Sikhs stopped Nur-ud-din near the Chenab; Sialkot's surrendered garrison was permitted to leave.
Allied chiefs relieved Charat at Gujranwala; Abed's siege collapsed and weapons, animals and stores were abandoned.
episodes.authored_theme: Gujranwala survived through coalition as well as its own fort
avoid: An unqualified assertion that no fighting took place
Presenting the narrator as an adult participant in 1761

episodes.summary: Durrani attacked the Sikhs and their families at Kup; Charat helped resist and protect the retreat amid devastating losses.
episodes.authored_theme: Remember the people lost and the obligation to protect families
avoid: A single casualty figure as an exact count

episodes.summary: Charat supported Hari Singh Bhangi expedition to Kasur; the city was taken and plundered.
episodes.authored_theme: A campaign account includes the war carried into other towns
avoid: An exact April or May attack date as settled
Presenting plunder as a bloodless relief or a documented private family lesson

episodes.summary: Charat participated at Sirhind but directed his territorial ambition toward the northwest rather than claiming land there.
episodes.authored_theme: Military success and subsequent choices are separate

episodes.summary: Charat fought in repeated Sutlej engagements; Afghan formations resisted, and Sikh forces withdrew and renewed their attacks as Durrani continued homeward.
episodes.authored_theme: Courage does not guarantee that an enemy's line will break
avoid: A single conclusive annihilating defeat inferred from repeated tactical withdrawals
An exact Machhiwara location presented as certain

episodes.summary: Charat and Gujar expanded into Jhelum and secured Rohtas; northwestern authority developed through conquest, local appointments and alliances.
episodes.authored_theme: Holding a place brings responsibility beyond taking its walls
avoid: Treating 1767 as the first-ever control of Rohtas
Merging Sarbuland's earlier two-lakh ransom into the later 1767 siege
Claiming all northwestern territories changed hands simultaneously

episodes.summary: During Jammu succession fighting, Charat died when his own gun burst. Desan managed the chiefship while Maha was young.
episodes.authored_theme: Loss brought a change of command and Desan carried its affairs
avoid: Choosing a death year or exact age of the young heir
Claiming the weapon was overcharged or ornamented, a commander was targeted, or the gun was held in a particular posture
Inventing a mound, tent, skull wound, last stand or pre-battle camp scene as attested detail

alternative_reports: Teja/Ganda p. 163 gives a lowest estimate of about 10,000

reported_quantities.claim: Sarfaraz ransom in final Rohtas conquest

reconciliation_notes.finding: Gupta II places an earlier capture and Sarbuland ransom within its 1764 campaign sequence. Gupta IV separately describes the May 1767 Jhelum campaign and final Rohtas capture with Sarfaraz. Nur Muhammad's 1765 text independently reports Charat holding Rohtas. The supplied article joins elements from the two sequences.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Preserve the separate reported episodes; the opening can mention 1767 Jhelum and Rohtas without attributing Sarbuland's ransom to that year.

reconciliation_notes.finding: Gupta IV says the governor fled without striking a blow. Gupta II and Teja/Ganda describe fighting, a proposed or actual night attack, and defections. Cunningham dates the relief later.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Use coalition relief and enemy withdrawal; keep September 1761 as the later synthesis's editorial caption, with the variant retained here.

reconciliation_notes.finding: The inspected cited Gupta II account includes failure to break lines, feigned retreat, renewed ambushes, both parties retiring at night and prolonged harassment. It also marks Machhiwara as probable and notes another historian's Rupar identification.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Describe contested fighting and withdrawals while the Durrani army continued its march; do not convert the sequence into an uncomplicated victory or definitive destruction.

reconciliation_notes.finding: Army sizes, deaths and ransom amounts are reported historical quantities rather than audited measurements.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Keep estimates in research metadata; the child's opening does not need numerical exposition.

reconciliation_notes.finding: Signed Punjabi University entries use 1770; Gupta IV pp.304-305 and Cunningham p.122 use 1774. The common bounded event is a fatal burst of Charat own gun during the Jammu succession conflict.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: No exact death year or young Maha age in dialogue; fixed 1792 Maha death remains untouched.

reconciliation_notes.finding: The signed Desan entry gives death 1778; Wikipedia gives 1794. Gupta IV p.305 calls her Maha stepmother, whereas the signed entry calls him their eldest son.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Use grandmother as family role and chiefship management; avoid a claim that Ranjit personally knew her and avoid biological mother adjudication.

reconciliation_notes.finding: Named Charat participation is supported. Signed encyclopedia uses April 1763; Gupta II describes the May heat.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Use only 1763 in opening, and retain taking and plunder rather than embellishing a bloodless rescue.

reconciliation_notes.finding: Cumulative AI conversations combine supported campaigns with highly specific unlocated action and direct speech. Some underlying episodes and one later-reported captive anecdote have inspected scholarly support.
reconciliation_notes.resolution: Retain each bounded claim and uncertainty in the candidate ledger; no automatic conversion to mission, inventory, animation, exact quotation or historical authority.

intake_policy.purpose: Retain user references and research candidates without expanding the ten-beat intro into an exhaustive campaign mission
intake_policy.coverage: Selective audit, not a claim to enumerate every skirmish in Charat Singh life
intake_policy.unlocated_means: Not located in inspected evidence, not proof that an event could never have occurred
intake_policy.admission_rule: Admit only the individually bounded historical claim; keep inferred choreography, purported quotations, quantities and identity-specific actions separate
